title: Check yourself: limitations of traditional enums

questions.stem: A shared library declares `public enum Region { EU, US }`, with no constant bodies. A customer needs an APAC region before the library's next release and writes, in their own code, `final class ApacRegion extends Region { }`, planning to pass an instance wherever a Region is expected. What happens?

options.text: javac refuses ApacRegion, since Region is implicitly final as long as none of its constants has a body of its own
options.says: an enum without constant bodies is implicitly final, and javac reports that enum classes are not extensible

options.text: javac refuses ApacRegion until Region gives a constant a body, since a body turns the enum into a sealed class open to subclasses
options.says: a constant body makes the enum sealed with only its own constant classes permitted; an outside class is still refused

options.text: It compiles, and values() lists the new instance once ApacRegion is loaded, since loading a subclass adds its instance to the enum
options.says: it doesn't compile; the constants listed in the enum are all the instances there are

options.text: It compiles, but values() and switch never see the new instance, since both know only the constants that Region itself declares
options.says: it doesn't compile: no class may extend an enum

origin.section: An Enum's Type Is Closed: It Can't Extend a Class, Take a Type Parameter, or Be Extended

questions.stem: A configuration module on Java 21 declares `enum Option<T> { RETRIES, ENDPOINT }`, hoping to give RETRIES an Integer value and ENDPOINT a URI value later. What does the compiler do with this declaration?

options.text: It refuses it, since an enum declaration has no place for a type parameter in Java 21 or in any release before it
options.says: javac reports 'enums cannot be generic'; JEP 301 proposed generic enums and was withdrawn

options.text: It refuses it on Java 17 but accepts it on Java 21, since generic enums arrived with the JEP that proposed them
options.says: JEP 301 was withdrawn; Java 21 still refuses a type parameter on an enum

options.text: It accepts it with an unchecked warning, since the type parameter is erased and every constant ends up holding an Object
options.says: the declaration is a compile error, not a warning; the rule is a language choice, not an effect of erasure

options.text: It accepts it, but every constant shares one type argument, since a type argument is given once for the whole enum type
options.says: the declaration doesn't compile at all

origin.section: An Enum's Type Is Closed: It Can't Extend a Class, Take a Type Parameter, or Be Extended

questions.stem: An enum `Unit { GRAM("g"), KILOGRAM("kg"); private static final Map<String, Unit> BY_SYMBOL = new HashMap<>(); ... }` has a constructor that stores its symbol and then calls `private static void index(Unit u) { BY_SYMBOL.put(u.symbol, u); }`. A service starts, and two requests in a row call `Unit.parse("kg")`. What do they get?

options.text: The first fails with ExceptionInInitializerError and the second gets KILOGRAM, since the JVM initialises the class again on its next use
options.says: a class whose initialisation failed is not initialised again; every later use gets NoClassDefFoundError

options.text: The first fails with ExceptionInInitializerError and the second with NoClassDefFoundError, since the JVM doesn't initialise the class again
options.says: BY_SYMBOL is still null when the constructors run, so initialisation fails, and the class stays failed

options.text: The first and the second both fail with a plain NullPointerException, since each call reaches the map before the map has been assigned
options.says: the NullPointerException happens once, inside class initialisation, and reaches the caller wrapped in ExceptionInInitializerError; later calls get NoClassDefFoundError

options.text: The first and the second both get KILOGRAM, since an enum's static fields are assigned before any of its constants are constructed
options.says: the constants are static fields declared first, so they are built while BY_SYMBOL is still null

origin.section: A Constructor Runs Before the Enum's Static Fields Are Assigned

questions.stem: A billing service keeps rates in an `EnumMap<Tariff, Rate>`, and picks a formatter by the value's class from a `HashMap<Class<?>, Formatter>` in which Tariff.class is registered. A developer gives `Tariff.NIGHT` a body that overrides `price()`. What changes for NIGHT?

options.text: Only the rate lookup misses it, since the EnumMap compares the key's runtime class with Tariff and the HashMap doesn't
options.says: EnumMap goes through the declared enum type, so a constant with a body is found like any other

options.text: Only the formatter lookup misses it, since the HashMap compares the runtime class with Tariff and the EnumMap doesn't
options.says: a constant with a body is an instance of an anonymous subclass, so getClass() is not Tariff.class; EnumMap is unaffected

options.text: Both lookups miss it, since both maps compare the runtime class with Tariff, and NIGHT's runtime class has changed
options.says: EnumMap, EnumSet, switch and instanceof treat a constant with a body like any other

options.text: Neither lookup misses it, since neither map compares the runtime class with Tariff, and NIGHT's runtime class hasn't changed
options.says: getClass() of a constant with a body is its own anonymous subclass; only getDeclaringClass() reports Tariff

origin.section: A Constant With a Body Is an Anonymous Subclass, So getClass() Isn't the Enum
